chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: 'Ornithology' and Benny Harris
summary: The tune came from a Bird phrase on 'How High the Moon' changes; Harris wrote it, and Bird's time was amazing.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: We were talking about chord patterns in "How High The Moon" and Bird, and that, of course, leads me to "Ornithology," which Benny Harris wrote...
Yeah.
...from a phrase that Bird played on the Jay McShann record of "The Jumpin' Blues." He took that phrase and made it into a tune based on "How High The Moon."
Right. Well, it fittted "How High The Moon" so easily, you know. Because it was running... You know, it was this running melody, and the chords was changing just
McGhee (12/6) - 23

right for that. It just laid nicely for him to write that thing there. And Bird was the first one that I heard play it, and it was beautiful then, you know, on 52nd Street, when he used to play down there with Benny Harris and all those guys.
Now, Benny Harris was never really known as a great soloist, but he...
But he had ideas.
But he wrote a lot of very interesting tunes that people liked to play.
Yeah.
What do you remember about Little Benny?

Well, first thing, let's get [SINGS 4 BARS OF 'ORNITHOLOGY'] I never will forget that. I know that he wrote that. And Bird... I mean, he really got it from Bird. But when Bird played it, it sounded like something else altogether different. But Benny wrote the music. Everybody gave him credit for that.
Well, he was probably one of the first of the young musicians around New York to pick up on...

But he didn't play...he didn't sound right. He didn't sound like that's what he would play, you know. I mean, he played all right, but it was one of those kind of things where it just didn't really lay out and say, "Well,
McGhee (12/6) - 24
this is the way like Bird laid it out." Bird laid it out so pretty and so golden that it was just there -- you couldn't deny it.
Bird's sense of time was I think...
Amazing.
Along with everything else he did. But to me, that... Everything was just perfect.
Yeah. Well, I think he was one of the few cats you could sort of say was perfect. Because Bird was something else. It's hard to believe that a man could be as brilliant as Bird has been in his music.
